page: Vultr vbm-72c-480gb-gh200-gpu is a dedicated bare-metal server configured for accelerated artificial intelligence and high-density compute tasks. It couples an ARM64-based NVIDIA Grace CPU with an NVIDIA Hopper GH200 graphics processing unit. The host incorporates 72 physical cores based on the Neoverse V2 architecture operating at 3.1 GHz with dedicated core mapping and one thread per core. System memory consists of 480.0 GB of RAM, yielding 6.67 GB per physical CPU core.

Hardware acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Hopper GH200 module equipped with 96 GB of unified VRAM. Local system storage consists of a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the platform includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The non-virtualized bare-metal structure eliminates hypervisor abstraction overhead, allowing direct hardware access across the processor, system memory, and accelerator.

Cost efficiency is centered on high computational density per chassis, leveraging the integrated Grace and Hopper architecture. While total capacity provides massive memory and tensor execution capabilities, local storage is limited to 960 GB, requiring external storage volumes for large datasets. This profile is engineered specifically for large language model inference, AI model fine-tuning, high-performance computing simulations, and data-intensive analytical pipelines.
description: Vultr vbm-72c-480gb-gh200-gpu is a bare-metal server tailored for hardware-accelerated computation and machine learning workloads. Powered by an ARM64 NVIDIA Grace processor with 72 physical Neoverse V2 cores clocked at 3.1 GHz, the system provides 480.0 GB of system memory, averaging 6.67 GB per core. Acceleration is handled by an integrated NVIDIA Hopper GH200 GPU featuring 96 GB of high-speed VRAM. Dedicated bare-metal provisioning eliminates hypervisor latency, offering full direct control over CPU and GPU resources. Local disk storage includes a bundled 960 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by a single public IPv4 address. The server represents an efficient, dense platform for workloads requiring unified processing throughput, such as large-scale model inference, deep learning model fine-tuning, complex physics simulations, and tensor-heavy technical computing.
